questions.question: In the supporting information, what does TEMPO refer to?
What solvent and temperature were used for the oxidative methyl esterification reactions (Typical Procedure I)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Solvent: DCE (1,2‑dichloroethane); Temperature: 50 °C (under O2 from a balloon, 48 h reaction time)

questions.question: What yield was reported for methyl palmitate (6ae)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Formed in 83% NMR yield (crude); isolated yield 73% (198.3 mg)

questions.question: In the compound labels on these pages, what does the abbreviation 'COOMe' refer to?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The methyl ester functional group: –COOCH3 (carboxylate ester with a methyl alcohol portion).

questions.question: What is the structure shown for compound 6oe (as printed on the page)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: EtO2C(CH2)5COOMe — i.e., EtO2C–(CH2)5–COOCH3 (an ethyl ester at one end and a methyl ester at the other).

questions.question: Between compounds 6fe and 6ke, which sample was reported to have the higher purity by NMR and what were the values?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 6ke had the higher purity: 98% for 6ke versus 96% for 6fe.
